$schema.description: The JSON Schema this config is written against. ocel init writes the schema shipped with the CLI that created it.

allowDegraded.description: The needs this project waives rather than have a deploy refused over.

apps.description: The apps this project deploys. Left off, ocel detects one at the project root.

arch.description: The processor architecture a serverless app's functions are built for. Left off, the provider's default architecture.

build.description: How a container app's image is built.

command.description: The command that builds the app inside the image. Left off, the app's own build script runs.

context.description: The directory the image is built from, relative to the project. Left off, it is the workspace root the app belongs to.

dockerfile.description: The Dockerfile to build from. A relative path resolves against the app's directory.

build.title: BuildConfig

compute.description: What the app runs on: serverless functions packed per route, or one container image serving everything.

domains.description: The hostnames this app is served on.

production.description: The hostnames production is served on.

domains.title: AppDomainConfig

entrypoint.description: The file the app is served from, when it is not the one ocel would detect.

folder.description: The variables folder this app reads, when it does not read the project's own.

framework.description: What a serverless app is built with, when ocel is not to read it off the app's own manifest.

health.description: How a container app is checked before it is served.

path.description: The path the check requests, off the app's own root. Any 2xx answer means up. Left off, the check requests /.

health.title: HealthConfig

name.description: The app's name. It is a label of every resource the app deploys and of its preview hostname, so it is a DNS label.

path.description: The app's directory, relative to the config.

bindings.description: Resources this project declares that ocel binds to a record your own infrastructure published, instead of provisioning them itself. Keyed by resource type, then by the name the app declares; the value is the name the record is published under. A name nothing has published refuses the deploy.

bucket.description: Each key is a bucket resource this project declares; its value is the name the record is published under.

postgres.description: Each key is a postgres resource this project declares; its value is the name the record is published under.

discovery.description: Where the resources an app declares are found.

paths.description: The directories holding infrastructure declarations, relative to the config. Left off, ocel reads the default discovery directory.

discovery.title: DiscoveryConfig

dns.description: Where the project's hostname records are written.

kind.description: The DNS the project's records are written into.

zone.description: The zone the records are written into. Omit it and ocel picks the zone that covers the hostname.

dns.title: DnsDescriptor

domains.description: The hostnames this project is served on.

preview.description: The wildcard hostname previews are served under, such as *.preview.example.com.

production.description: The hostnames production is served on.

domains.title: ProjectDomainConfig

edge.description: The edge in front of the origin. Omit it and the provider fronts the deployment with its own default edge.

kind.description: The edge the project's hostnames are served from.

edge.title: EdgeDescriptor

provider.description: The provider ocel deploy provisions into.

name.description: The provider's name — the one ocel fetches, runs and deploys through.

options.description: The options this provider takes. The provider itself is what checks them.

provider.title: ProviderDescriptor

registry.description: Where this project's container images are pushed.

password.description: The name of the environment variable holding the password or token — not the secret itself.

server.description: The registry host and the namespace images sit under, such as ghcr.io/acme. No scheme, and no credentials.

username.description: The username the push authenticates as, where the registry wants one.

registry.title: RegistryConfig

slug.description: The project's deployment identity. Every stack and resource ocel creates in your own account is keyed on it, so changing it forks a new project.

transforms.description: Transform modules applied while provisioning, in order — later modules win where their patches collide. Each is a path to a module whose default export is a defineTransform(...) result, keyed by the provider it patches.
